[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/01/13 (Fri) 15:08.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) released its Sixth Assessment Report, warning that the world has about a decade to take drastic action to limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Human activities are unequivocally causing climate change, and the consequences will be catastrophic if urgent action isn't taken.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Record-breaking heat waves have occurred in North America, Europe, and Asia, leading to devastating wildfires in Greece, Turkey, and the western United States.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Extreme rainfall events have caused severe flooding in Germany, Belgium, China, and India, with climate change leading to more frequent and intense precipitation events.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] A study published in Nature found that sea levels are rising at an alarming rate, primarily driven by the melting of glaciers and ice sheets and the thermal expansion of seawater.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Arctic ice cap has reached a record low for this time of year, with some areas experiencing ice-free conditions.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Researchers have warned that the world is approaching several climate tipping points, including the collapse of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet and the die-off of coral reefs.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] A study published in The Lancet found that climate change is responsible for thousands of deaths worldwide, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The 26th Conference of the Parties (COP26) is scheduled for November 2021 in Glasgow, Scotland, where world leaders will discuss climate action plans.
